title: Heterogeneous GPU slot allocator & attention micro-tiler (H100/L40S/A10)
creator: Ariana Patel
description:
Problem: In mixed-sku clusters (H100 / L40S / A10) with MIG partitions we observe periodic latency spikes and throughput variability for prefill-heavy chat workloads. Root causes from telemetry: (1) microbatches misaligned with slice affinity leading to NVLink/NIC hot spots, (2) attention kernel churn when sequence-length distributions vary across concurrent requests, and (3) abrupt GPU clock domain changes under opportunistic scaling that invalidate selected kernels. This ticket implements a combined slot allocator and attention micro-tiler to stabilize kernel selection and reduce cross-slice contention.

Goals / success metrics: target 95th-percentile tail latency reduction of 12-20% on mixed-sku clusters for our chat benchmark; improve steady-state throughput by ~8-12% (tokens/sec per reserved GPU); reduce per-token cost variance during bursty prefill by >= 6%. Maintain median latency within 5% of baseline.

Proposed approach (high level):
1) Slot allocator: introduce a per-node "slot map" that aligns incoming microbatches to MIG slices and their preferred clock domain. The allocator groups requests by (sequence length bucket, model variant, affinity-tag) and assigns them to time-slot ranges that preserve KV-cache locality. This reduces slice-crossing and NVLink saturation.
2) Attention micro-tiler: implement a small runtime pass that inspects the request's sequence-length histogram and selects an attention tiling strategy (e.g., row-major tile vs. strided tile) and microbatch packing width. The tiler emits a kernel_hint tag consumed by the kernel selector to prefer kernels optimized for that tiling shape.
3) Clock-smoothing adapter: when the allocator detects frequent clock domain flips (from telemetry), we apply a damped clock-hint that instructs the kernel selector to prefer non-fragile kernels during the smoothing window and avoid narrow-latency kernels that regress heavily if clocks change.
4) Kernel selector integration: extend the kernel selector ranking with a new score component for (slice-affinity + tiler-hint + clock-stability) to reduce thrash. Add a configurable hysteresis so kernel swaps occur only when a sustained throughput/latency improvement is predicted.

Trade-offs and decisions:
- Grouping microbatches by affinity reduces schedule packing flexibility; we will keep a soft budget allocator to reclaim unused slots to avoid wasting GPU cycles.
- Preferring stability-oriented kernels may slightly increase median latency but reduces tail variance; will tune the hysteresis window based on real-world telemetry.

Telemetry & metrics to add:
- New gauges: slot_fill_ratio per MIG slice, kernel_hint_mismatch_count, clock_flip_rate (per-minute).
- Traces: annotate request traces with assigned_slot, tiler_strategy, selected_kernel, kernel_swap_reason.
- Dashboards: migration-specific panel showing p50/p95/p99 by affinity-tag and model variant.

Testing plan:
- Microbench harness: extend our multi-sku harness to replay production sequence-length distributions and simulate noisy clock events.
- Unit tests: deterministic allocator behavior, tiler strategy selection for edge histograms.
- Staging rollout: A/B with conservative traffic fraction on dedicated pools (start 5% -> 20% -> 50%).

Rollout & rollback:
- Feature flag gate at allocator and looser kernel-swap threshold.
- Runtime config knobs to revert to original allocator and kernel scoring without deploy.
- Rollback criteria: if p95 worsens by >5% or error rate increases >0.5% on canary.

Files / PRs / design artifacts: Confluence design, perf harness, and initial prototype PRs linked below.

Open questions:
- Best default sequence-length bucketing scheme for multi-tenant workloads (fixed power-of-two buckets vs. learned buckets). We'll run a short experiment to compare.
- Interaction with existing KV cache eviction heuristics — allocator may need to surface expected cache residency durations to the cache manager.

Notes: This ticket focuses on runtime scheduling and kernel selection policy; it does not change low-level CUDA kernels themselves (except for passing the kernel_hint metadata).

2026-02-25 Marcus Chen: Prototype allocator implemented (branch: alloc/microtiler). Early local runs show slot_fill_ratio improvements but some throughput regression when buckets are too narrow. Added adaptive reclamation to address wasted slots.

2026-03-02 Marcus Chen: Attention micro-tiler v1 added. On H100 heavy tail sequences, p95 improved ~14% in replay harness for model-7b. L40S shows smaller gains (~6%). Need to tune tiler thresholds per-SKU.

2026-03-06 QA: Stress test with simulated clock jitter (rapid frequency governor changes) produced a 9% p95 improvement when clock-smoothing enabled. Also observed one regression case where median increased by 3% for extremely short sequences — will add a bypass for short-seq fast-paths.
2026-03-09 PR review comments: @sre requested additional tracing for kernel_swap_reason and suggested exponential backoff for kernel re-evaluations. Addressing in next commit.
